anchor: shared runtime loader boundary between samples/zigux/runtime_* and zigux/kernel/runtime_loader.zig

gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 9 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the runtime survey family machine-checkable without inventing a runtime loader implementation.
A dedicated survey gate keeps the mixed Phase 6 schedule wording, the real Phase 9 roadmap target, and the missing runtime-loader seam explicit on current master.
The repo already had runtime starter samples and two loader-plan files, but it still lacked one shared note that says Phase 6 should not absorb runtime allocator or init-flow work.

The bitmap and kretprobe starter lanes already publish entry and exit symbol names, requires_runtime_substrate flags, selftest-hook markers, and handoff-stage checks that a future shared runtime loader must consume.

The roadmap's first command and environment plumbing surfaces live in Phase 8 tooling, but the current runtime starter family still has no shared runtime control surface that records command-name, argv-policy, or environment-derived activation handling.
The allocator policy surface exists, but no shared runtime loader consumes it yet, so allocator ownership, fallback rules, and failure cleanup stay unbound to runtime module bring-up.
A shared init and exit consumer is still missing, so the staged entry and exit symbol names published by the sample-side loader plans cannot become a real runtime lifecycle path.
